title: Strictly Palindromic Number
statement: Call an integer `n` *strictly palindromic* when, for every base `b` from `2` up to `n - 2` (both ends included), the digits of `n` written in base `b` form a sequence that is the same left to right as right to left. Given `n`, return `true` if it is strictly palindromic and `false` if it is not.
notes:
## Intuition

The direct method writes `n` in every base from 2 to `n - 2` and checks each digit string, about O(n log n) work. A little algebra makes that unnecessary: `n = 1 · (n - 2) + 2`. When `n >= 5` the base `n - 2` is at least 3, so `2` is a legal digit and `n` is written `12` in that base, which is not a palindrome. When `n = 4` the only base is 2, where `4` is `100`, also not a palindrome. So no allowed `n` is strictly palindromic and the answer is always `false`. The reference still builds the witness base so you can watch the argument happen.

## Approach

1. Set `base = n - 2`, the base the algebra points to.
2. Peel off digits with `% base` and `/ base`, storing them in `digits` (least significant first).
3. Compare `digits` from both ends with `left` and `right`; the first mismatch proves `n` is not strictly palindromic, so return `false`.
4. The math guarantees a mismatch; the final `return false` only documents that.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 9`, so `base = 7`. `9 % 7 = 2` and `9 / 7` rounds down to `1`, then `1 % 7 = 1` and `rest` becomes `0`. `digits` is `[2, 1]`, which is `12` read from the top. `left = 0`, `right = 1`: `2 !== 1`, so the answer is `false`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(1): `n` has at most three digits in base `n - 2`.
- Space: O(1): `digits` holds at most three values.

## Pitfalls

- Checking only one base and returning `true` when it is a palindrome is wrong in general; one palindromic base proves nothing, one non-palindromic base proves `false`.
- `n = 4` is the special case: base 2 cannot use the digit `2`, so its form is `100`, not `12`.
- A brute force must use `b <= n - 2` inclusive; base `n - 1` would always give `11`, a palindrome.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `base` | the witness base `n - 2` |
| `digits` | digits of `n` in that base, lowest first |
| `rest` | the part of `n` not yet turned into digits |
| `left`, `right` | the two ends being compared |
